breadcrumbs.current: Trade and Commerce with the Outside World

hero.title: Sangam Trade and Global Connectivity
hero.description: An analytical exploration of South India's maritime dominance, Roman trade relations, and the economic landscape of the Sangam Age.

timeline.title: The Chronological Framework
timeline.description: Key phases of maritime interaction during the Classical Age.

cards.details: Early mentions of Southern kingdoms (Chera, Chola, Pandya) in Ashokan inscriptions.
The Periplus of the Erythraean Sea documents the peak of Indo-Roman maritime trade.
Ptolemy records major ports like Puhar and Muziris in the global maritime map.

mnemonics.title: Mnemonics for Ports
mnemonics.description: Remember the primary ports associated with Sangam dynasties.

items.title: M.C.P.
items.decryption: Muziris (Chera), Puhar (Chola), Korkai (Pandya). Use this to align kingdoms with their trade gateways.

traps.title: UPSC Common Exam Traps
items: Confusing 'Puhar' (Chola) with 'Korkai' (Pandya). Remember: Puhar is Kaveripattinam.
Assuming Roman trade was limited to luxury goods; it included significant agrarian and craft produce.
Thinking Sangam trade was only maritime; inland trade routes existed connecting the coast to the interior (Madurai).

sections.title: 1. Core Study Notes
sections.content:
Geography

  • Malabar Coast: Pepper source
  • Coromandel Coast: Pearl fishery
  • Arikamedu: Indo-Roman hub

Commodities

  • Exports: Pepper, Spices, Pearls
  • Imports: Gold coins, Wine, Amphorae

Economic Structure

  • Guilds (Vanigar): Organized merchant groups managing trade
  • Currency: Roman Aurei and Denarii found in hoards (e.g., Coimbatore)
  • Trade Centers:
    • Muziris (Muchiri)
    • Arikamedu (Poduke)
    • Kaveripattinam (Puhar)
PortDynastyMain Export
MuzirisCheraPepper (Yavanas-priya)
PuharCholaCotton Textiles
KorkaiPandyaPearls
